A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BTD-sampling research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot RL experiments on Cheetah, Walker, and Quadruped, including benchmark comparisons, sampling ablations, and empirical signal-dilution measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an empirical study of the number of subtrajectories used to fit the behavioral task distribution.

M1.justification: Task-vector extraction, GMM fitting, and BTD-based policy training remain unchanged. Section 4.2 now explicitly describes subtrajectories as contiguous consecutive transitions; this clarifies the existing procedure rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ExORL RND datasets and four test tasks each for Cheetah, Walker, and Quadruped. The added subtrajectory-count sweep changes sample sizes within this coverage, without adding environments or tasks.

E2.justification: The seven representation baselines, offline TD3 oracle, and Table 2 sampling comparators are retained. The new experiment studies FB with BTD across sample counts without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: New Appendix E.4 evaluates FB with BTD while varying the GMM fitting sample count from 10 to 1,000,000 subtrajectories. Existing training settings in Table 1 and the 5,120-state test-task inference protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.4 adds a sensitivity analysis asking how many subtrajectories are needed for effective GMM estimation and downstream performance. Existing sampling-strategy, signal-dilution, and mixture-component analyses remain; the previous UMAP analysis moves to E.5.

E5.justification: Both versions state that reported results are averaged over five seeds. Existing error bars and Table 2 uncertainty values are retained, with no new seed-count disclosure, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test.

E6.justification: New Figure 7 reports sample-count sensitivity curves for FB with BTD, showing performance largely plateauing around 10,000 subtrajectories across the three environments. Existing result figures and Table 2 values are unchanged; these are additional results, not revised same-setting performance scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds an explicit assumption that the MDP is fixed and independent of representation dimension d in the asymptotic argument. Proposition 4.1, its variance identity, and the remaining derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims remain uniform-sampling signal dilution, method-agnostic BTD integration, and an average 20% performance improvement. The new introduction contribution list summarizes claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: A new limitations paragraph identifies underrepresentation of rarely observed behaviors, emphasizes the linear-reward restriction, and marks generalization beyond locomotion as untested. Appendix E.4 also interprets the sample-count plateau as sufficient behavioral coverage and motivates an estimation-quality versus computational-cost tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses a default of 10,000 subtrajectories and identifies IDRIS computing resources. It removes v1's promise to release code upon acceptance without supplying replacement access information. The default disclosure does not establish that existing experiments used a changed setting.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Tirinzoni et al. on FB-based expert-policy distillation and Bobrin et al. on adaptation across dynamics. The Ledoux concentration-of-measure citation is removed. The broader positioning relative to SF/FB, adaptive goal sampling, and IRL remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds contribution bullets, limitations, an impact statement, and acknowledgments, alongside localized wording clarifications and conference publication text. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a three-panel sample-count sensitivity plot as Figure 7. The existing UMAP plot is relocated and renumbered Figure 8. All seven original graphics and both table structures are retained, with surrounding text reflow.

improvement.justification: The new sample-count study supports and documents the 10,000-subtrajectory default, while explicit applicability limits and the fixed-MDP assumption improve transparency. These are useful, bounded gains with the central method and existing results unchanged. Removing the planned code-release statement weakens release transparency, but the added evidence and qualifications support a modest net improvement.
